_README: HAND-CAPTURED DISCLOSURES for the Alpha Signal.
Every figure in this file was read from the primary source named beside it and
typed in by hand, on the date in `capturedAt`. Nothing here is modelled,
estimated or derived from anything other than the cited page — the same rule
assets/data/summaries.json follows for earnings-call summaries, and for the same
reason: the app ships no scraper and no model, so a fact that needs a human to
read it says so and carries the link.
WHAT THIS FILE IS FOR. Six of the eleven Alpha Signal categories have gaps that
no FMP endpoint can fill: consensus estimate revisions, backlog, patents and
launches, job postings, search interest, and corporate actions. Where a primary
source publishes the fact for free, it is captured here so the category can be
scored instead of reported dark.
WHAT IT IS NOT. It is not a feed. It does not update. Every entry is frozen at
`capturedAt` and the UI prints that date beside anything built from it. A symbol
with no entry here shows the gaps exactly as before — nothing is defaulted,
extrapolated from another company, or carried over.
TO REFRESH OR EXTEND: tools/capture/README.md lists the source URL and the
query behind every field, so each one can be re-read and re-typed. Replacing
this file with a real provider integration is the intended end state; the
shape below is deliberately close to what such a provider would return.

AAPL.capturedBy: Read by hand from the sources cited on each block.

source.title: AAPL Analyst Estimates — EPS Trend and EPS Revisions

estimateRevisions.note: Consensus EPS as it stood at four points in the past, which is the series FMP does not publish. Basis is GAAP as displayed.

source.title: Apple Inc. Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended September 27, 2025

backlog.note: The word "backlog" does not appear anywhere in Apple's FY2025 Form 10-K. The company does not disclose it, so there is no figure to omit — this is a measured absence in a primary source, not a missing data feed.

nearestDisclosed.name: Total deferred revenue
nearestDisclosed.quote: As of September 27, 2025 and September 28, 2024, the Company had total deferred revenue of $13.7 billion and $12.8 billion, respectively.
nearestDisclosed.realisation: 66% expected within one year, 23% within one-to-two years, 9% within two-to-three years, 2% beyond three years.
nearestDisclosed.why: Deferred revenue is the contract-liability disclosure required under ASC 606. It is the closest thing Apple publishes to a forward order book, and it is not the same measurement as backlog.

purchaseObligations.note: Manufacturing purchase obligations cover forecast component and manufacturing requirements, typically for periods of up to 150 days.

source.title: Granted US patents, assignee Apple Inc.

patents.note: Counts of granted US patents by publication date, assignee Apple Inc. Family members outside the US are excluded so one invention is counted once per jurisdiction rather than ten times.
patents.lagWarning: Patents publish months after grant and the index lags further, so the newest window always undercounts and is marked unsettled. Only the two settled windows are compared.

source.title: Apple Newsroom — press releases and updates

launches.note: Dated, company-published product and commercial events. Announcement text only — no judgement about commercial significance is recorded here.

events.title: Mac mini with M6 and M5 Pro, and Mac Studio with M5 Max and M5 Ultra, available
Apple opens Apple Music Hall, a live music venue in London
The latest iPhone, Apple Watch and AirPods lineups arrive in stores worldwide
Celebrating “What Holds Us” on iPhone 18 Pro
Widow’s Bay most decorated freshman comedy in Emmy history
Major updates for Apple’s software platforms now available

corporateActions.note: Declared dividends, as published by the company. Amounts are not split adjusted.

source.title: Search interest for “AAPL”, United States, past 12 months

searchInterest.note: Weekly relative search interest, 0-100, where 100 is the peak week of the window. It is an index, not a count, and it is comparable only within this series.

jobPostings.reason: Apple's careers site reports “600+ Result(s)” and returns that same capped figure for every team and location filter, exposes no per-function facet counts, and its search API rejects unauthenticated requests. A capped total that does not move with the filter carries no information, so nothing is recorded rather than a number that looks like a measurement.
jobPostings.wouldNeed: A job-postings provider (LinkUp, Revelio, or direct ATS ingestion), which would also have to be labelled postings rather than hiring.
